_doc: No Justice: the script for the voiced lines (#807). The same shape as sheriff_road.json (its _doc and docs/scripts/README.md say the fields). Nothing is built of this mission yet, so every trigger says what it will need. Nothing here is approved until Sean taps Script OK. Since 2026-11-17 (#1056): written to the house style, docs/story/DIALOGUE.md. `when` names the StoryState fact a line waits on (the top-level `facts` list says which exist and which gameplay has to add); `was` holds a line's wordings before the rewrite; `added` marks a new line. The mission is built now (config/moments/no_justice_camp.json, _hideout.json, _cabin.json, said as this script had them): a wording here that differs from the game's has status new and is listed for gameplay in docs/scripts/CHANGES.md.
title: No Justice
mission: no-justice (built to its four endings, #966; the jail and the release are not built)
status: rewritten 2026-11-17 in the house style (#1056): waiting on Sean's Script OK again
sources: docs/missions/no-justice.md (Sean's card of 2026-11-09, on PR #743's branch)
docs/story/OUTLINE.md Act I, VOICES.md (Joe, the doctor, Kett, the bold cowboy), SETUPS.md, WORDS.md (A Southern Ute man; rule 7) (PR #833)
#830: C4 a (the raid was provocation; the costume stays), C5 b (the cabin ends Kett's crew), C8 a (the release: P until Sean nods), C13 b (slurs), C14 c
notes: Harlan doesn't speak: he answers Joe with the nod and the shake, and by what he does.

Joe: English is his third language (WORDS.md). Exact, plain, few contractions, says a thing once. Never 'heap', 'many moons', dropped verbs or speeches about the land. His talk with the survivors is in Ute and is not written here: a Southern Ute speaker or not at all.
Nobody says Kett's name (K3, who names him is open). His crew call him 'Red', a cowhand's nickname by look (WORDS.md).
Where Joe and Harlan meet is open (s3); the card says the doctor's office, so that's where it's written. The bold cowboy's part is open (s4): his one line is the card's.

Rule 7 (slurs, Kett one of three men allowed, at a moment that matters): one moment is marked (cabin.bargain) and written without the word. Sean decides whether it gets one; the word is chosen then, and may not be voiceable.
Rewritten 2026-11-17 (#1056). Sean's lines stay word for word: 'Are you going to stop me?', 'Is that a yes?', 'That was mine to take.'

Joe is a man whose wife was murdered, and he talks about horses, dogs, a hat and what her mother will ask. He never says what he feels. 'It is done' and 'It did not give her back' are gone for that reason.
The town remembers: lines with an 'If:' wait on what you did (carried the sheriff or left him, sat at Earl's table, went out after Cody). Joe has heard all of it.
Kett has been in the state prison at Cañon City and rates jails by their supper. He has seen Joe's face at the cabin, so in the arrest ending the costume has not held with him.

words_to_check.worry: Checked 2026-11-17: De Vere (1872) has it from California, 'Were both men heeled?' Keep.
'Yellow' for cowardly: given as 1856 in American use (ref). To check before voicing.
The Spanish card game, common in Colorado and New Mexico. Period; keep.

setups.status: P: C8 a waits on Sean's nod

setups.what: The outbreak that wasn't (the costume spoils it)
Who sent them (a hint only: Kett offers it, never says it)
Harlan's past (Kett on his knots: 'The Army?')
The foreman's face (Kett offers to sell who sat with you)
Harlan is a steward (Joe has heard)

cast.name: Joe
cast.bible: VOICES.md, Joe; WORDS.md, A Southern Ute man
cast.brief: Thirties to forties (O), a Southern Ute man; English his third language after Ute and Spanish. Low, exact, unhurried; long quiet, dry humour. Not a film Indian: no stately cadence, no accent played for effect. Cast with care; a Native voice actor if there's ever a choice.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner; brisk, quiet, dry.

cast.name: The bold cowboy
cast.bible: VOICES.md, Smaller voices (s4: his part is open)
cast.brief: Thirties, a Texas hand; plain, blunt, unimpressed by anybody; says the ugly thing because it's true.

cast.name: The red shirt (Silas Kett)
cast.called: nobody names him; 'Red' to his crew
cast.brief: Thirties, a drummer's easy patter on a gunman; light, friendly, quick. Wheedles and whines when cornered; a coward's voice that cracks. Has done time at Cañon City; talks like a man selling something even with his hands tied.

cast.name: Kett's crew (one)
cast.brief: Twenties to thirties, a Texas hand; hard and loud in a fight.

cast.name: Kett's crew (two)
cast.brief: Forties, older and rougher, gravel voice; the one who sees Red run.

cast.name: Rourke's officer
cast.bible: VOICES.md, Rourke; WORDS.md, Soldiers (C8 a, P)
cast.brief: Late twenties, a regular officer, Eastern, correct and cold; whole sentences, never loud.

scenes.title: The doctor's office
scenes.when: After Harlan's sworn (s3: where they meet is open)
scenes.setting: A man in grief in a room you walk into; no quest marker. Joe, the doctor, the bold cowboy. The doctor warns that the killers won't be punished, and the cowboy agrees. Harlan agrees to ride with Joe (a nod).

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.trigger: You come into the doctor's office; Joe is there
lines.delivery: Quiet, to you, a glance at Joe. He stops himself telling the rest.

words.text: Harlan. This is Joe. Riders came through his people's camp the night Earl was shot, with the men off hunting. His wife... she's dead.

was: This is Joe. The night Earl was shot, his people's camp was raided while the men were out hunting. His wife was killed. I'll not tell the rest. He can, if he chooses.

lines.speaker: cowboy
lines.trigger: From the corner, when you come in
lines.when: nolaw.seen_from = table (you sat at Earl's table)
lines.delivery: Doesn't look up from rolling his smoke. Says it to the room.

words.text: That's the one sat at Earl's table. Sat right there.

lines.note: A callback: the saloon followed him here. It makes Joe's question about the badge bite.

lines.speaker: cowboy
lines.trigger: From the corner, when you come in, in place of doctor.cowboy_table
lines.delivery: Doesn't look up. A fact about you, laid on the table for Joe.

words.text: He's the one carried Earl up here. Still got him on his coat.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Very level. No heat in it at all, which is what makes it frightening.

words.text: I want the men who did it.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: A real question; he's watching your face for the answer.

words.text: You wear the sheriff's badge. Does it do anything?

lines.speaker: doctor
lines.delivery: No pleasure in saying it; a man who's sat on juries.

words.text: Bring them in if you like. I never yet saw a white man hang on an Indian's word.

lines.speaker: cowboy
lines.delivery: From the corner, not looking up. He isn't arguing. He has sat in that saloon.

words.text: A jury? They'd stand him a drink.

was: Doc's right. No jury in Colorado'll hang a white man for a Ute woman. I've seen 'em try.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Once. He won't ask twice.

words.text: I'm going today. You coming?

was: I ride today. Will you come?

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Already at the door.

words.text: Good. Get your horse.

was: Then we go now.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: No reproach. He expected it, and goes.

words.text: No. ... All right.

lines.note: the card has no 'no' path yet: Joe goes alone?
was: No. I did not think so.

scenes.title: Joe's camp
scenes.when: The same day, the Southern Ute camp
scenes.setting: The raid's damage still there: burned belongings, bullet holes. The survivors tell Joe what happened, in Ute (not written: a Southern Ute speaker or not at all). Joe tells Harlan, in English, what they said.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Getting down from his horse; a hand up to keep you back.

words.text: Wait here.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: He comes back from the survivors
lines.delivery: A list. If he stops on any of it he won't go on.

words.text: Six men. One says seven. They shot the dogs first. We were four days out, after elk.

was: Six of them. Seven, one says. They came in the night. We were four days gone, hunting. Four days.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: The one thing they saw. Flat. He is fixing it in his own head.

words.text: The one who did it to her wore a red shirt. Old. The red gone out of it. Nobody saw his face.

was: The one who did it to her wore a red shirt. Faded. That is all they saw of him. It is enough.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: A plain fact.

words.text: They rode for the hills. That way.

was: They went toward the hills. That way.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.when: nolaw.followed (you followed Cody out of the saloon)
lines.delivery: He noticed you weren't surprised. Not a question.

words.text: You saw them ride out.

was: You knew that already.

scenes.title: The ride
scenes.when: The foothills, on the raiders' trail
scenes.setting: Joe changes into a cowboy's hat and neckerchief and says why. He leads, reading the trail. They talk a little, without long stops.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Before they ride, he puts on the hat and neckerchief
lines.delivery: Tying the neckerchief. Plain, as if it were obvious.

words.text: A Ute kills a white man, the whites burn the camp. So today I'm a cowboy.

was: If they see a Ute, they go to the camp after. If they see a cowboy, they come to me.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: If you look at him a while in the hat
lines.delivery: If you look at him a while in it. Dead level. It is the only joke he makes all day.

words.text: I won this hat at monte, from a Texas man. He said it was a good hat. He lied about the cards, too.

was: A hat and a rag at my neck, and I am nobody's Indian. Only one more man who shot at them.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Reading the ground, every so often on the trail
lines.delivery: Half to himself; short.

words.text: Six horses. One throws his right fore.
They watered here. Took their time.
These are fresh. An hour.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Out of nowhere, looking ahead. 'Do', not 'did'. Then nothing more.

words.text: She shot better than I do. She told everybody.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.when: sheriff.care = good (you packed the sheriff's wound)
lines.delivery: A fact he has collected about you. Not a compliment.

words.text: The doctor says you know wounds. One of us will want that.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Once, on the trail, in place of ride.carried
lines.delivery: He has heard the freighter's story in town and worked out the name. Said once, looking at you.

words.text: They say the sheriff called a name from the road, and the man kept walking. ... Don't walk off from me.

lines.note: A callback: what you did on the road has reached Joe.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Plain. He is giving you the chance to turn back, without saying so.

words.text: When we have him, don't watch.

was: When I find him, you will not like what I do. Better you know it now.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: On the hillside above the hideout
lines.delivery: A whisper; counting them.

words.text: Five. Six. There. By the fire. The red shirt.
How do you want it? Creep in, or shoot from here?

was: How do you want it? Quiet, or now?

scenes.title: The hideout
scenes.when: The fight at the gang's camp
scenes.setting: Five or six men, the end of Kett's crew (C5 b). Harlan chooses how it starts: creep in, or open fire. Joe fights beside him. At the first shots, or as it turns, the red shirt runs for the cabin and bars himself in, plain to see. Lines that can repeat have two or three wordings.

lines.speaker: crew1
lines.trigger: They see you, or the first shot
lines.delivery: Shouted, grabbing a rifle.

words.text: Riders! On the hill!
Somebody's out there!

was: We got company!

lines.speaker: crew1
lines.trigger: In the fight, a man calls where you are
lines.delivery: Short and loud.

words.text: Behind the woodpile!
There's only two of 'em!
By the wagon! Get him!

lines.speaker: crew2
lines.trigger: A man of the crew is hit
lines.delivery: Pain and fury.

words.text: I'm hit! God damn it!
My leg! Jesus!

lines.speaker: crew2
lines.trigger: The red shirt breaks for the cabin
lines.delivery: Yelled after him, as much contempt as fear.

words.text: Red! Where you going? Red, you yellow son of a bitch!

lines.speaker: crew1
lines.delivery: Throwing his gun down.

words.text: I quit! Don't shoot!

was: I'm done! Don't shoot!

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe in the fight, calling targets
lines.delivery: Short, steady; never shouting more than he must.

words.text: Left. By the wagon.
Two. Behind the logs.
Red shirt's running! The shack!

was: The red shirt. He runs.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe is hit and goes down
lines.delivery: Through his teeth; angry at the leg, not afraid.

words.text: My leg. Go on. Go on!

was: I am hit. The leg. Go on.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Shaking you off as soon as he's standing.

words.text: It's all right. I can walk.

was: Enough. I can walk.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: You kill the red shirt outside, before the cabin
lines.delivery: Not shouted. Cold, close; then he walks past you to the body.

words.text: That was mine to take.

scenes.title: The cabin
scenes.setting: Harlan forces the door (a kick, or through a wall), Joe close behind. The red shirt is cornered, frightened and unarmed; he surrenders and begs to be taken in. Joe draws his knife and asks if Harlan is going to stop him. The nod answers: nod, I'll stop you; shake, I won't. Stepping between them, drawing on the man or walking out answer too.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: Too high, too fast; the bluff of a man with no gun.

words.text: Stay out! I got a gun! I'll use it!
I'll shoot through the door! I will!

was: First man through that door gets it!

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: Hands up, backing into the corner; grabbing at the badge as a lifeline.

words.text: I'm done! I ain't heeled! You're law, ain't you? Then take me in!

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: Babbling, a hand waved at the bodies outside. The salesman's mouth still running with nothing to sell.

words.text: It weren't only me. Ask them. Ask any of them. Hell, they're dead, ain't they. It weren't only me.

was: It weren't only me. Ask them. It weren't only me.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe draws his knife and walks to him
lines.delivery: He takes the cowboy's hat off first and lets it drop. Very quiet. To the man, not to you.

words.text: Look at me. You were at my camp.

was: You know me. You were at my camp.
lines.note: Was 'You know me': Kett has never seen him; Joe was four days out hunting. The hat coming off is where the costume ends (gameplay: the hat, and nojustice.kett_saw_joe).

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: The patter back, desperate: selling the one thing he has.

words.text: You'll want to hear who sent me, Deputy, before that Indian opens my throat.

lines.note: Rule 7's moment, if Sean wants one: Kett showing what he is, with the knife at him. Written here without a slur; the word is Sean's call.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.trigger: After cabin.bargain, when Harlan hasn't moved
lines.when: nolaw.seen_from = table (you sat with the stranger)
lines.delivery: Faster. He has remembered something he can sell.

words.text: I know you. You're the one he sat with. I can tell you who he is, Deputy. Him at your table. His whole business.

lines.note: A hint only: he never says it. K11 and K14 stay shut.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: He turns to you, the knife ready
lines.delivery: Looking you in the eye. Waiting.

words.text: Are you going to stop me?

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: He wants it said plainly, with your head.

words.text: Is that a yes?

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: He puts the knife away slowly. Cold. It is the question he asked in the doctor's office.

words.text: Take him. Go on. See what your badge does.

was: Then take him. Take him to your law. We will see what it does.
lines.note: Pays off doctor.badge ('Does it do anything?').

lines.speaker: kett
lines.delivery: The fear going out of him too fast; the patter back before his hands are down.

words.text: Bless you, Deputy. Bless you. I always did say a town wants law. I'll come quiet as a lamb.

was: Bless you, Deputy. You're a fair man. I'll come quiet.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: You shake your head: you won't stop him
lines.delivery: Not looking at you. He doesn't want you to see it.

words.text: Go outside, Harlan.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Wiping the blade on the man's own shirt. An order, flat. Then nothing for a long time.

words.text: Get the horses.

was: It is done.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Staring at you, not the body. A statement, not a question.

words.text: He had his hands up.

scenes.title: The ride back
scenes.setting: Revenge: they ride back together; Joe quieter, nothing mended. Arrest: the prisoner on a horse between them, Joe plainly unhappy, Kett talking.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: To the road ahead. What he doesn't say is the rest of the line.

words.text: Her mother'll ask me is it finished. I'll tell her it is.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.trigger: On the ride back, every so often
lines.delivery: Friendly; a man selling something. Each on its own, a while apart.

words.text: They'll not keep me, Deputy. You know that, don't you?
Fine country. Be a shame to leave it.
Who learned you to tie a man like this? The Army?
I've rode in worse company. Not a deal worse.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.delivery: Not to Kett. To you. An offer, and he means it.

words.text: I can gag him.

was: He talks a great deal for a man with his hands tied.

scenes.title: The jail and the release
scenes.when: Salt Creek, the arrest ending (C8 a: P until Sean nods)
scenes.setting: Kett sits a couple of days in Harlan's jail. Then the train brings Rourke's officer with a paper: a crime against a Ute woman on the reservation is the United States' matter, not the county's. Harlan hands him over on the platform, and the officer turns him loose for want of a witness the court will hear. Later Kett walks Main Street.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.trigger: In the cell, when you come by
lines.delivery: On the cot, hat over his eyes. Cañon City is the state prison; he says it like a hotel.

words.text: Couple of days, Deputy. That's all this is.
Somebody'll come. They always do send somebody.
What's supper? ... I ate better in Cañon City.

lines.speaker: officer
lines.trigger: Off the train, on the platform, to you
lines.delivery: Holding out the paper; courteous and immovable.

words.text: Deputy, I have an order for your prisoner: a crime on the reservation is a matter for the United States and not for the county.

lines.speaker: officer
lines.trigger: On the platform, the prisoner handed over
lines.delivery: Not even to you: to the paper. Then he cuts the cords.

words.text: There is no witness a court will hear. The man is at liberty.

lines.speaker: joe
lines.trigger: Joe hears of it, or sees it
lines.delivery: No anger left to show. He isn't saying he was right.

words.text: Doc told us. In his office.

lines.speaker: kett
lines.trigger: You meet him on Main Street after the release
lines.delivery: Tipping his hat. Enjoying it. The third only if he saw Joe's face at the cabin: it is a threat.

words.text: Morning, Deputy. Fine day to be at liberty.
Still here, Deputy?
Say good morning to your Indian for me.

facts.values: up / down (he was hit at the hideout)
true: Joe took the hat off at the cabin and Kett lived
facts.set_by: gameplay to add, with the hat coming off at cabin.knife
used: street.kett; whether the kin go to the camp (S12)

kept.words: Are you going to stop me? / Is that a yes? / That was mine to take.
kept.why: Sean's lines (2026-11-09), word for word. The blind reader heard 'Is that a yes?' as present-day. A period way, if Sean wants one: 'Is that yes?'

kept.words: I'm hit! / There's only two of 'em!
kept.why: Barks in a gunfight: plain on purpose.
